title: huff0: static decompression buffer (up to ~30% faster)

source.license_note: Real upstream klauspost/compress optimization PR #499; measured-speedup task.

task.summary: Speed up huff0 4X decompression by replacing the per-call stack [256]byte temp buffer with a reusable static [4][256]byte buffer on the Decoder and indexing it per-stream in the hot decode loops, without changing decoded output.
task.instructions: Optimize the huff0 package for speed WITHOUT changing behavior. The benchmark BenchmarkDecompress4XNoTable measures it; existing tests must still pass.
task.acceptance_notes: Behavior preserved (go test passes); higher measured speedup is better. Do NOT edit any *_test.go.

code_fault.description: huff0 4X decompress paths allocate a fresh [256]byte temp buffer per call and index it with offset arithmetic (bufoff*stream) instead of using a reusable static [4][256]byte buffer with direct per-stream indexing.

ops_fault.description: huff0 Decompress4X / decompress4X8bit / decompress4X8bitExactly use a per-call stack [256]byte temp buffer and offset-based indexing in the inner decode loops, leaving speed on the table on the hot decompression path.
detection_keywords: per-call temp buffer in huff0 decode loop
offset arithmetic indexing in hot loop
repair_keywords: local pointer vars br1/br2 in decode loop

visible_context.issue_text: huff0 4X decompression is slower than it needs to be: each call allocates a stack temp buffer and uses offset arithmetic to index it within the tight per-stream decode loops.
visible_context.notes: Real upstream optimization PR; no fabricated profiling numbers.
